hooks.prompt:
This repo keeps a friction log — /ast-grep-rules:lesson records one in about thirty seconds — so that mistakes worth preventing can become enforced ast-grep rules.

Below is one file edit, as JSON. Judge that edit alone; you cannot see the conversation, so do not guess at it.

Answer ok=true, reason "ordinary edit", for forward progress: new code, a rename, a changed string or number, formatting, comments, added tests, or extending something that already worked. That is the common answer and it stays silent. When in doubt, answer ok=true.

Answer ok=false only when the diff plainly takes work back: code removed with nothing put in its place, or one construct swapped for a structurally different one — a class for a function, require for import, an untyped value for a typed one. For that answer, name in the reason what was taken back and what replaced it, then close with: if this followed a correction, offer /ast-grep-rules:lesson before moving on, so the cause is recorded while it is fresh — one entry, and the user decides. The entry belongs in this repo's own friction log and nowhere else; a lesson written to a memory store or a scratch note is not recorded, because /ast-grep-rules:mine never reads those. If that file cannot be written, say so rather than putting the entry somewhere it will not be found.

$ARGUMENTS
hooks.statusMessage: checking whether that edit is worth a lesson
